events.table_description: This table stores user interaction events within the Jupiter Money app, tracking user engagement and onboarding processes.

columns.description: A unique identifier for each event recorded in the log.
A unique identifier for each user interacting with the app.
A unique identifier for each user session, tracking user activity within a single session.
The name of the event that occurred, indicating the type of user interaction.

value_meanings.dob_entered: User entered their date of birth
value_meanings.vkyc_call_completed: User completed the video KYC call

columns.description: The category of the event, indicating the broader context of the user interaction.
The exact date and time when the event occurred.
The date when the event occurred, formatted as YYYY-MM-DD.
The hour of the day when the event occurred, in 24-hour format.
The day of the week when the event occurred.
The platform on which the app was accessed (e.g., Android, iOS, Web).
The version of the app that the user is using.
The city where the user is located.
The state where the user is located.
The type of account the user has with Jupiter Money.
The age range of the user.
The income range of the user.
The occupation of the user.
The source from which the app was installed.
Indicates whether a referral code was used during installation.
Indicates if this is the user's first time opening the app.
The time in hours since the user last opened the app.
The number of notifications received by the user.
The number of actions pending for the user to complete.

suggested_metrics.name: Average Time Since Last Open
suggested_metrics.description: This metric measures the average time users take to return to the app after their last session, indicating user engagement and retention.

suggested_metrics.name: First Open Rate
suggested_metrics.description: This metric indicates the percentage of users who are opening the app for the first time, which is crucial for understanding onboarding success.
suggested_metrics.sql_hint: COUNT(DISTINCT user_id WHERE is_first_open=true) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT user_id WHERE event_name='app_install'),0)

suggested_metrics.name: Referral Code Usage Rate
suggested_metrics.description: This metric shows the percentage of new users who used a referral code during installation, reflecting the effectiveness of referral marketing.
suggested_metrics.sql_hint: COUNT(DISTINCT user_id WHERE referral_code_used=true) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT user_id WHERE event_name='app_install'),0)

suggested_metrics.name: App Open Rate
suggested_metrics.description: This metric measures the frequency with which users open the app, indicating overall user engagement.
suggested_metrics.sql_hint: COUNT(DISTINCT user_id WHERE event_name='app_opened') / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT user_id WHERE event_name='app_install'),0)

suggested_metrics.name: Transaction Completion Rate
suggested_metrics.description: This metric indicates the percentage of initiated transactions that are successfully completed, which is vital for assessing the transaction process.
suggested_metrics.sql_hint: COUNT(DISTINCT user_id WHERE event_name='transaction_reconciled') / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT user_id WHERE event_name='transaction_initiated'),0)

suggested_metrics.name: Average Notifications Received
suggested_metrics.description: This metric measures the average number of notifications received by users, which can help assess the effectiveness of communication strategies.

suggested_metrics.name: Pending Actions Rate
suggested_metrics.description: This metric shows the average number of pending actions per user, indicating potential friction points in the user experience.

events.description: This event captures when a user inputs their Aadhaar number during the onboarding process.

This event signifies that the user has successfully verified their Aadhaar number using the OTP.

The number of attempts made to verify the OTP.

users.table_description: This table stores information about users of the Jupiter Money neobank, including demographics, account details, and engagement metrics.

columns.description: A unique identifier for each user. This column is never null.
The date and time when the user signed up for the service. This column is never null.
The platform through which the user accessed the service, such as Android, iOS, or web. This column is never null.
The version of the app used by the user. This column is never null.
The city where the user is located. This column is never null.
The state where the user is located. This column is never null.
The age range of the user, categorized into buckets. This column is never null.
The income range of the user, categorized into buckets. This column is never null.

value_meanings.10-20L: Users with an income between 10 to 20 Lakhs
value_meanings.20L+: Users with an income above 20 Lakhs
value_meanings.3-6L: Users with an income between 3 to 6 Lakhs
value_meanings.6-10L: Users with an income between 6 to 10 Lakhs
value_meanings.<3L: Users with an income below 3 Lakhs

columns.description: The occupation of the user. This column is never null.

value_meanings.salaried_govt: User is employed in a government job
value_meanings.salaried_private: User is employed in a private job

columns.description: The marketing channel through which the user was acquired. This column is never null.

value_meanings.app_store_seo: Acquired through app store search engine optimization

columns.description: Indicates whether the user has completed the Know Your Customer (KYC) process. This column is never null.
The type of account the user holds with the neobank. This column is never null.
The primary bank associated with the user's account. This column is never null.
The number of sessions the user engages in per week. This column is never null.
The average amount of transactions made by the user. This column is never null.

suggested_metrics.name: Average Transaction Amount Per User
suggested_metrics.description: This metric measures the average transaction amount for each user, providing insights into user spending behavior.

suggested_metrics.name: KYC Completion Rate
suggested_metrics.description: This metric indicates the percentage of users who have completed the KYC process, which is crucial for regulatory compliance.
suggested_metrics.sql_hint: SELECT COUNT(*) / NULLIF(COUNT(user_id), 0) FROM users WHERE kyc_completed = true

suggested_metrics.name: Sessions Per User
suggested_metrics.description: This metric measures the average number of sessions per user, indicating user engagement with the platform.

suggested_metrics.name: User Distribution by Age Bucket
suggested_metrics.description: This metric shows the distribution of users across different age buckets, helping to understand the demographic profile.
suggested_metrics.sql_hint: SELECT age_bucket, COUNT(*) FROM users GROUP BY age_bucket

suggested_metrics.name: User Distribution by Income Bucket
suggested_metrics.description: This metric shows the distribution of users across different income buckets, providing insights into the economic demographics of users.
suggested_metrics.sql_hint: SELECT income_bucket, COUNT(*) FROM users GROUP BY income_bucket

custom_events.name: activated_user
custom_events.description: Users who have completed the onboarding process and verified their identity.

custom_events.name: active_user
custom_events.description: Users who have opened the app at least once within the specified time window.

custom_events.name: paying_user
custom_events.description: Users who have successfully completed a transaction.

custom_events.name: churned_user
custom_events.sql: event_name IN ('app_opened') AND date < DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE, INTERVAL 30 DAY)
custom_events.description: Users who have not opened the app in the last 30 days.

custom_events.name: referral_user
custom_events.description: Users who installed the app using a referral code.

glossary.description: Number of unique users who opened the app on a given day.
glossary.sql: COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) WHERE event_name = 'app_opened' GROUP BY DATE(timestamp)

glossary.description: Number of unique users who opened the app in the last 30 days.
glossary.sql: COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) WHERE event_name = 'app_opened' AND date >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE, INTERVAL 30 DAY)

glossary.description: Percentage of users who completed the onboarding process out of those who installed the app.
glossary.sql: (COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) WHERE event_name = 'onboarding_completed') / (COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) WHERE event_name = 'app_install') * 100

glossary.description: Estimated revenue generated from a user over their lifetime.
glossary.sql: SUM(amount) WHERE event_name = 'transaction_reconciled' AND transaction_status = 'SUCCESS' GROUP BY user_id

glossary.description: Percentage of users who have not engaged with the app in the last 30 days.
glossary.sql: (COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) WHERE event_name = 'app_opened' AND date < DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE, INTERVAL 30 DAY)) / (COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) WHERE event_name = 'app_install') * 100

conventions: Default time window: last 7 days unless user specifies otherwise.
Date grouping is done by day.
